prompt:
Image 1 is a pixel-art sprite sheet of the upper body of a small chibi knight for a top-down 2D game doing a flat horizontal sword slash in four frames, from the front, the side and the back. Image 2 shows the same knight running in two diagonal views. Create ONE NEW sheet of the same upper body doing the same slash in the two diagonal views of Image 2. The blade sweeps a half circle around the knight, level with the ground, from the knight's right side, through the front, to the knight's left side. Keep exactly the same character, armour, helmet, size, proportions, palette, sword, shield and pixel-art style, on the same flat solid pure magenta background, RGB 255,0,255.

Upper body only: the helmet, head, shoulders, torso, both arms, the sword and the shield, stopping at the belt. There is no skirt, no legs and no feet.

Layout: exactly 2 rows and 4 columns, one upper body per cell, with clear magenta space around each one so that nothing touches.

The most important rule: within a row, only the sword arm and the sword move. The helmet, the head, the torso, the shield arm and the shield are identical in all four columns of that row, in exactly the same place. The shield never changes sides and never moves.
In row 1 the shield is always on the right side of the picture.
In row 2 the shield is always on the left side of the picture.

Row 1: seen from the front-right diagonal, turned towards the viewer and to the right, exactly like row 1 of Image 2. The sword is in the hand on the left side of the picture.
Column 1: the sword arm is stretched out to the lower left, and the blade points to the lower left.
Column 2: the sword arm reaches forward and down, and the blade points straight down.
Column 3: the sword arm reaches forward across the belt, and the blade points to the right and slightly down.
Column 4: the sword arm has swung across the chest, the hand in front of the shield, and the blade points to the upper right, passing in front of the shield.

Row 2: seen from the back-right diagonal, turned away from the viewer and to the right, exactly like row 2 of Image 2. The sword is in the hand on the right side of the picture.
Column 1: the sword arm is stretched out to the lower right, and the blade points to the lower right.
Column 2: the sword arm reaches forward on the right side of the picture, and the blade points to the right and slightly up.
Column 3: the sword arm reaches up beside the helmet, and the blade points straight up.
Column 4: the sword arm has swung across behind the helmet, and the blade points to the upper left.

In every frame the fingers are tightly closed around the sword's handle and the blade is a straight extension of the hand, so that the arm and the sword move together as one piece. The sword must be fully visible and must not be cut off.

Do not include: legs, feet, a skirt, text, labels, numbers, grid lines, ground, shadows, dust, motion lines, slash effects, borders, watermark, or any other object. No soft gradients, blur or painterly rendering.
